question: Which Rajput princess belonged to the Bhakti tradition of Medieval India, whose songs were devoted to Lord Krishna?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mirabai.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mira Bai's** profound devotion to Lord Krishna was the defining essence of her life.
 
• She regarded Krishna as her Divine Lover and expressed her intense love through heartfelt songs and poems.
 
• Born around **1498 in Kudaki, India**, Mira Bai belonged to the **Rajput royal family**. Her upbringing encompassed a diverse education in music, religion, politics, and governance.
 
• Despite societal conventions and expectations, Mira Bai embarked on a path of spiritual devotion, prioritizing her connection with Krishna over conforming to traditional roles.
 
• She devoted much of her time to her personal temple dedicated to Krishna, where she immersed herself in composing songs filled with love and yearning for the Divine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Muddupalani **was a Telugu-speaking poet and a devadasi affiliated with the court of Pratap Singh, the Maratha king of Tanjore.
 
• **Lalleshwari,** also known as Lal Ded, was a Kashmiri mystic associated with the Kashmir Shaivism school of Hindu philosophy. She pioneered the style of mystic poetry called vatsun or Vakhs, which translates to "speech."
 
• **Akka Mahadevi **emerged as one of the early poets of Kannada literature and played a significant role in the Lingayat Shaiva sect during the 12th century.
